Describe a drawing hall in a Cairo college building, pick one of the thesis interventions and set its parameters, and see what it does to energy, thermal comfort, daylight and CO₂. Built from the simulations of the PhD thesis on the architecture design studio of Cairo University.

Each intervention's selected design, against the studio as built

The design picked by the thesis selection rule (least distance to the ideal point, equal weights), compared with the studio as built on the same floor. The air-conditioned cases are compared with the air-conditioned reference. Click a row to open it.

ProjectApproach to enhance indoor environmental quality of architectural halls in college buildings in Egypt. Case: Architecture Design Studio, Faculty of Engineering, Cairo University.
DataFinal simulation runs of 24 Sep–1 Oct 2026: EnergyPlus at six timesteps per hour, Radiance on a 1.0 m grid of 896 sensors with the real glass (VT 0.88). CO₂ for every design from the 9 Oct 2026 re-runs (an EnergyPlus contaminant balance, outdoor air 420 ppm, 108 students), which reproduce the published energy and comfort figures. Orientation: the hall grid with the sun turned every 45°, and every intervention's selected design simulated at each step (13–14 Oct 2026).
Reading the numbersThesis studio tab: every value is a simulated result. Your hall tab: the plain hall is interpolated between simulated halls, and the intervention's change is simulated on the studio or, where marked, on halls like yours. Comfort is the share of counted hours (Sat–Thu, 07–19) outside the ASHRAE 55 adaptive band, or outside PMV ±0.5 when air-conditioned. Differences under 0.2 UDI points or 2 sDA points are within Radiance noise.
